about.title: Livingston Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Three people died on Livingston's streets in 2025, and behind each of those numbers is a family in Merced County trying to figure out what comes next. If that is your family, you do not need a lecture on the legal system right now. What you may need is a clear path to someone who can carry the legal weight while you grieve. Livingston is a small city of about 13,900 people, and its collision reports cluster along a few familiar routes: Hammatt Avenue, Walnut Avenue, F Street and Main Street. Records also show crashes tend to peak on Friday afternoons between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m. Not every fatal loss involves a vehicle. Wrongful death claims in California also arise from workplace incidents, unsafe premises, defective products and medical negligence. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases on contingency, meaning no attorney fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What Livingston Families Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Only certain relatives can bring the claim
items.desc: California limits who has standing: a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out who in your family is eligible so the claim is filed correctly the first time.

items.title: The two-year clock starts on the date of death
items.desc: Most wrongful death actions in California must be filed within two years of the death, and the window is far shorter when a government entity may be responsible. Reaching out early protects the option to act.

items.title: Losses go beyond the funeral bill
items.desc: California allows families to recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. An independent attorney can help document each of these fairly.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The law puts a surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children of the person who died at the front of the line. If there is no one in that group, certain financially dependent relatives or heirs may be able to bring the claim instead. Because standing is limited, it helps to confirm eligibility with an attorney before anything is filed.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on a Livingston city street. Does that change the deadline?
items.answer: It might. The general deadline for a California wrongful death action is two years from the date of death, but if a city, county or state agency may share responsibility, for example over the condition of a road like F Street or Main Street, a much shorter administrative claim deadline applies. Speaking with an attorney soon after the loss keeps every possible avenue open.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we still need a separate civil case?
items.answer: Yes, they are two different processes. A criminal case in Merced County is brought by prosecutors to punish the wrongdoing; a wrongful death claim is a civil action your family brings to recover your own losses. The civil claim can move forward whether or not the criminal case results in a conviction.
